To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We have used a novel integrated approach combining X-ray crystallography and X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy to determine the three-dimensional structure of the copper centre of azurin at atomic resolution and to study the changes that occur in the metal centre upon oxidation-reduction.
the Cu-S(3) bond is elongated by 0.08 A upon reduction, whereas the other Cu-S bonds are shortened.

the Cu site of oxidized azurin contains a Cu2+ ion with a distorted tetrahedral coordination, whereas in the reduced form of the same protein the Cu ion is in a square-pyramidal environment with a Cu(I) oxidation state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of electron transfer in metalloproteins, in particular the role of the protein in the electron transfer process.
the study of the structural properties of biological systems, with particular reference to the metal centres of proteins, by using X-ray absorption spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction.
the elucidation of the structural changes which take place at a metal site when it is involved in a redox process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cu-S bond length in reduced azurin (1.98 A) is significantly shorter than that in oxidized azurin (2.05 A), whereas the Cu-S bond angles remain unchanged.
the Cu-S bond lengths in azurin change by 0.1 A upon reduction.
the Cu site in the reduced form of azurin is more symmetric than the Cu site in its oxidized form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to define a structural model for the Cu centre of the reduced protein which is in excellent agreement with EXAFS data and is consistent with the crystallographic model of the oxidized protein.
the Cu site in the reduced form of azurin is slightly more distorted than in the oxidized form.

we have demonstrated that the Cu-S(Cys112) bond length increases by 0.06 +/- 0.01 A upon oxidation of azurin, whereas all the other Cu-S bonds remain essentially unchanged (within the experimental uncertainty).
The main takeaway from our work is that
EXAFS is an extremely powerful tool to obtain 3D structural information on the metal site in metalloproteins.
the Cu-S(Cys112) bond is elongated by 0.06 A in the reduced form.
the Cu site in the oxidized state is not a perfect tetragonal site.
